note: Canonical exercise library for the Train Today iOS app. Step text is preserved verbatim from the original web app; only timing metadata has been added.

steps.text: Jog in place for 1 minute to get your heart rate up.
High knees: lift each knee up to your belly button while jogging, for 30 seconds.
Butt kicks: kick your heels up toward your butt while jogging, for 30 seconds.
Leg swings: hold a wall or fence, swing each leg forward and back 10 times.
Arm circles: big circles forward 10 times, then backward 10 times.
Hip circles: hands on hips, make big circles with your hips, 10 each way.
Lateral shuffles: side-step quickly back and forth, for 30 seconds.
Drop the ball, let it bounce once, then kick it up with the top of your foot (laces). Catch it. Repeat.
Once you feel comfortable, try to kick it twice before catching it.
Keep your foot flat when you kick. Imagine your foot is a shelf the ball sits on.
Count your best streak! Write it down and try to beat it tomorrow.
If you get good, try alternating feet: right, left, right, left.
Set up 5 cones (or water bottles, shoes, anything!) in a straight line, about 3 feet apart.
Dribble through them using only the inside of your foot. Go slow and controlled first.
Come back through using the outside of your foot.
Rest 30 seconds, then repeat. Try to go a little faster each set.
Bonus: time yourself and try to beat your record!
Stand about 6 feet from a wall or rebounder.
Pass the ball firmly against the wall with the inside of your foot.
Control the return with your opposite foot. Soft touch!
Try 20 passes with your right foot, then 20 with your left foot.
Move back a few feet once you're comfortable and repeat.
Set up a goal (use cones or pick a spot on a wall/fence).
Start 10 feet away. Shoot using your laces and make sure you follow through!
Take 10 shots from straight on, then 10 from the left side, then 10 from the right.
After each shot, jog to get the ball. Don't just walk!
Try aiming for corners (low left, low right) instead of straight at the middle.
Toss the ball up in the air about head height. Let it drop.
Stop the ball dead with the sole (bottom) of your foot before it bounces twice.
Then try stopping it with the inside of your foot.
Do 15 reps each foot. The goal is a soft, controlled touch, not kicking it away.
Challenge: toss higher and try to chest-trap it, then foot trap before it bounces.
In an open space, dribble forward tapping the ball with the inside of your right foot, then the outside.
Inside tap, outside tap, inside tap, outside tap. Keep a rhythm.
Do this for 20 yards, then turn around and come back.
Repeat 4 times, then switch to your left foot.
This improves your ball control and makes you harder to defend.
Set up 2 cones: one where you start, one 10 yards ahead.
Run hard to the cone, then cut sharply to the right (out route). Raise your hands like you're catching.
Jog back. Repeat, this time cutting to the left.
Do 6 reps each direction. Focus on planting your outside foot hard before cutting.
Advanced: add a third cone and practice a corner route. Go straight, then cut out at 45°.
Toss a football up and catch with just your fingertips, not your palms.
Run 5 yards, turn around, catch a toss. Eyes on the ball the whole time, not the catcher.
Try catching while looking away, then turning at the last second.
10 catches straight on, then run routes and catch: 5 cuts left, 5 cuts right.
Remember: catch the ball, THEN tuck it in. Don't tuck early!
Set up 4 cones in a square about 5 yards apart.
Sprint forward to the first cone, shuffle sideways to the second, backpedal to the third, shuffle back to start.
This is called a 4-corner drill. It's used by real NFL players!
Do 4 rounds, resting 30 seconds between each.
Try to keep your hips low and stay on the balls of your feet. No flat-footed running!
Find a flat area: a backyard, street, or park works great.
Mark a start and end point about 30-40 yards apart.
Sprint as FAST as you can from one end to the other.
Walk back slowly. This is your rest.
Do 8 sprints total. Rest 45 seconds after every 2 sprints.
Gear up: helmet on, no shortcuts!
Ride at a comfortable pace for the first 5 minutes to warm up your legs.
For the middle 10 minutes, try to go a little faster. You should be breathing harder.
Cool down the last 5 minutes at an easy pace.
Try to explore a slightly different route each time!
Set up 4 cones in a line: 5 yards, 10 yards, 15 yards, and 20 yards from your start.
Sprint to the first cone, touch it (or the ground), sprint back to start.
Sprint to the second cone, back to start. Then third, then fourth.
That's 1 full suicide. Rest 45 seconds and repeat.
Try to complete 3-4 suicides. These are tough, so give everything!
No ladder? Use chalk or tape on the ground to make 10 boxes, each about 18 inches.
Run through stepping one foot in each box as fast as you can.
Try lateral shuffles: step side to side through each box.
Try the in-in-out-out pattern: both feet in, both feet out the sides, repeat.
Rest 20 seconds between each pass. Do 3 passes of each pattern.
Find a sturdy box, step, or ledge about 12-18 inches high.
Stand about 1 foot in front. Bend your knees, swing your arms back.
Explode up: swing arms forward, jump, and land SOFTLY on top with bent knees.
Step back down (don't jump down). Reset and go again.
Do 8 jumps, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 times. LAND SOFT, no loud thuds!
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees and swing arms back.
Jump as FAR forward as you can. Use your arms to help propel you.
Land softly with both feet, knees bent like a shock absorber.
Mark where you landed. Try to beat your distance each jump!
Do 6 jumps, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 times.
Stand on your right foot. Bend your knee slightly.
Jump sideways to the left, landing on your LEFT foot only. Balance for 1 second.
Then jump back to the right, landing on your RIGHT foot. That's 1 rep.
Keep your chest up and land soft. Pretend the floor is hot!
Do 8 total bounds, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 times.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly out.
Lower into a squat with thighs parallel to the ground and chest up.
Explode up and jump as high as you can!
Land softly back in the squat position. Don't let your knees cave in.
Do 10 jump squats, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 sets.
Start in a plank: hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Lower your chest to just above the ground. Keep elbows at a 45° angle, not flared wide.
Push back up to start. That's 1 rep.
Keep your core tight the whole time. No sagging hips!
Do 10, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 sets. Can't do 10? Do 5 on your knees. That's great too!
Start in a push-up position with arms straight and body flat like a board.
Drive your right knee toward your chest, then quickly switch: left knee in, right leg out.
Keep alternating fast, like you're running in place horizontally.
Keep hips down. Don't let your butt stick up in the air.
Go for 20 seconds, rest 20 seconds. Repeat 3 times. It should burn!
Find a sturdy chair, bench, or low step. Sit on the edge.
Put your hands next to your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your butt off the edge, legs out in front with knees slightly bent.
Bend elbows and lower yourself down until elbows reach 90°.
Push back up to start. That's 1 rep. Do 10, rest 30 seconds, 3 sets.
Get in push-up position. Drop to your forearms with elbows under shoulders.
Body should be straight from head to heels, like a wooden plank.
Squeeze your belly button toward your spine. Don't hold your breath!
Hold for 30 seconds. Rest 20 seconds. Repeat 3 times.
Too easy? Lift one foot off the ground to make it harder.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed out slightly.
Stretch your arms out in front for balance.
Sit back and down like you're sitting into a chair. Chest stays up!
Lower until thighs are parallel to the ground (or as low as comfortable).
Drive through your heels to stand back up. Do 12, rest 30 seconds, 3 sets.
Stand up straight. Drop hands to the floor, jump feet back to a plank.
Do one push-up (or skip it if you're tired).
Jump feet back to your hands, then explode up: jump and clap overhead!
Land soft, immediately go into the next one.
Do 6, rest 40 seconds, repeat 3 sets. These are HARD but make you super athletic!
Stand tall, feet together. Step your right foot forward about 2 feet.
Lower your back knee toward the ground. Front thigh should be parallel to the floor.
Push up through your front heel and bring your back foot forward. That's 1 rep.
Keep your chest up and don't let your front knee go past your toes.
Do 10 lunges each leg, rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 sets.
Squat down like you're sitting in a low chair, thighs about parallel to the ground.
Keep your chest up and hands out in front (or on your hips) for balance.
Waddle forward one small step at a time, staying low the whole way — like a duck!
Walk 15 yards forward, then waddle backward 15 yards to reset.
Rest 30 seconds, repeat 3 times. Burns your legs but builds serious hip and knee control.
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart. Hold a wall or chair if you need help balancing.
Toes pointing straight ahead: rise onto your tiptoes as high as you can, then slowly lower. Do 15 reps.
Turn your toes OUT (heels together, like a V) and do 15 more.
Turn your toes IN (pigeon-toed) and do a final 15. Different angles hit different parts of your calf!
Rest 30 seconds between each set of 15. Go slow on the way down — that's where the real work happens.
Stand on your right foot, arms out to your sides like airplane wings.
Hold as still as you can for 30 seconds. Pick a spot on the wall to stare at — it helps!
Switch to your left foot and hold for 30 seconds.
Level up: try closing your eyes for 10 seconds on each foot.
Level up more: bend your standing knee slightly and hold 30 seconds each leg.
Do 2 full rounds (both legs, all challenges).
Stand sideways to the direction you're going to travel. Pick a 15-20 yard path.
Cross your right foot OVER your left, then step your left foot out to the side.
Next cross your right foot BEHIND your left, then step your left foot out again.
Keep alternating over-behind-over-behind as you travel sideways. Hips stay facing forward the whole time.
Go 15-20 yards, then switch directions and lead with your left foot going back.
Do 4 total passes (2 each direction), moving a little faster once you feel confident.
Find a straight path: a driveway, sidewalk, or field works great.
Mark a 50-yard distance (about 45 steps).
Sprint at full effort from one end to the other.
Walk back slowly. This is your rest period.
Do 6 sprints. Rest 1 minute after every 2 sprints. Focus on FORM: drive your knees up, pump your arms!
A-skips: march forward with an exaggerated knee drive, skipping. 20 yards.
B-skips: same as A-skips, but kick your leg out at the top. 20 yards.
High knees: sprint in place driving knees as high as possible, for 20 seconds.
Butt kicks: sprint in place kicking heels to your butt, for 20 seconds.
Straight-leg bounds: jump forward off alternate feet with straight legs. 20 yards. Rest, repeat 2x.
Quad stretch: stand on one leg, pull your other heel to your butt. Hold 20 seconds each leg.
Hamstring stretch: sit on the ground, legs out, reach toward your toes. Hold 30 seconds.
Hip flexor stretch: kneel on one knee, lean your hips forward. Hold 20 seconds each side.
Seated butterfly: sit with feet together, press knees toward the ground. Hold 30 seconds.
Shoulder cross: pull one arm across your chest, hold with the other. 20 seconds each arm.
Child's pose: kneel and reach arms forward, rest forehead down. Hold 30 seconds. Breathe slow!
Hip circles: hands on hips, make big slow circles, 10 each direction.
Pigeon pose: from push-up position, bring right knee to right wrist, extend left leg back. Hold 30 seconds.
Switch legs. Hold 30 seconds.
Deep squat hold: feet slightly wider than hips, squat all the way down, hold for 30 seconds.
Lateral lunge stretch: step wide right, bend right knee, keep left leg straight. Hold 20 seconds each side.
